title: Introduce regional reroute insulator and TTL safeguard to prevent routing fanout spirals
creator: Priya Singh
description: Summary: After the 2025-11-03 capacity incident we observed repeated cross-region reroutes that amplified into a fanout spiral and caused sustained capacity amplification on warm pools. Root cause analysis points to stale policy snapshots + TTL miscoordination + lack of a short-lived dedupe/circuit-breaker layer in the router. This ticket scopes implementing a lightweight 'reroute insulator' service and TTL safeguard rules: a regional in-memory dedupe of routing decisions, explicit per-route short circuit-breakers (backoff windows), and a policy-ttl enforcement layer to prevent replaying stale policy snapshots during transient leader elections. The goal is to reduce re-fanout amplification by >90% in reroute storms and eliminate cascading capacity burns during short network flaps.
acceptance_criteria: Deploy insulator to canary region and confirm dedupe reduces duplicate reroute RPCs by >=90% in synthetic storm tests
Circuit-breaker prevents >3 immediate reroutes per route in a 60s window unless manually overridden
Policy TTL enforcement prevents application of policy snapshots older than configured threshold (default 30s) during control plane leader transitions
No observable increase in request tail latency (p95 change <= 5ms) after insulator enabled
Runbook updated with steps to bypass/toggle insulator and rollback criteria
implementation_notes: Prototype insulator as stateless sidecar with small in-memory LRU keyed by (tenant, route, last-decision-hash)
Use bounded timers + token-bucket backoff to implement short circuit windows (configurable: window=60s, allow=3)
Integrate insulator telemetry with existing routing trace: emit decision_hash, dedupe_hit, breaker_state, and TTL_source
Add policy snapshot version and timestamp propagation on control-plane changes; router will reject snapshots older than policy_ttl_threshold
Add feature flag 'routing.insulator.enabled' for staged rollout and kill-switch in console
comments: 2025-11-12 - Priya Singh: Created ticket after postmortem review; initial scope covers both dedupe + TTL enforcement. Linked Confluence design and initial prototype PR.

2025-11-14 - Daniel Park: Completed prototype sidecar that dedupes by decision hash and emits dedupe_hit counter. Observed 87% reduction in duplicate reroute RPCs in local sim. Pushed draft PR for review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1498

2025-11-17 - Emily Zhao (Reviewer): Suggestion to prefer LRU with time-decay instead of strict LRU to avoid state blowup for high-card routes. Also asked for additional metrics: per-tenant dedupe rate and breaker activation count.

2025-11-18 - Daniel Park: Incorporated feedback; switched to hybrid LRU+time-decay and added tenant-scoped metrics. Updated PR. Noted performance microbenchmark showing p95 +2ms over baseline in worst-case path.
2025-11-20 - Reliability WG (notes): Need explicit experiments for leader failover without insulator to quantify differences. Action: run controlled leader-swap experiment in staging on 2025-11-24.

2025-11-24 - Daniel Park: Ran leader-swap staging test. Without insulator: reroute RPCs spiked 8x and capacity burn observed on cold pools. With insulator: reroute spike limited to 1.3x and no capacity overload. Uploaded graphs to dashboard link in attachments.
2025-11-25 - Security (Anna Li): Reviewed architecture; no new data plane vectors. Recommended a short write-up for SRE on how insulator state is stored and potential impacts for paged workloads.

2025-11-26 - Priya Singh: Moving to In Progress -> Preparing canary rollout plan. Daniel to open canary deployment PR and ops runbook update. Next steps: feature-flagged canary in us-west-2 with 2% traffic, monitor dedupe_hit, breaker_state, token-bucket refill metrics, tail latency, and capacity burn signals for 48 hours. If metrics stable, progress to 25% and then full rollout.

Follow-ups: Add automated e2e test in CI to simulate leader flapping and assert no more than 2 reroutes per route per 60s window. Create alert: routing.insulator.breaker_activation > 50 in 5m -> Paging and escalate to oncall routing-owner.
